competitors.name: Visa Inc
competitors.why: Named in MA 10-K Item 1 as the first general purpose payments network competitor; the same issuers, acquirers, merchants and cardholders, same four-party card network model, same cross-border and value-added services (fraud, authentication, data) markets. Larger by volume and revenue.

metrics.fy2026_note_operating_margin: derived 28,110 / 45,900 from the release (about 45.9B rounded); GAAP, includes litigation provisions of 1,764M
metrics.forward_PE_gap: no forward P/E from a primary or structured source in this lane

competitors.name: American Express Co
competitors.why: Named in MA 10-K Item 1 as a general purpose payments network competitor; a closed-loop network and card issuer competing for the same premium consumer and commercial spend and for merchant acceptance. Revenue includes interest and card fees, so it is not a pure network.

competitors.name: PayPal Holdings
competitors.why: Digital wallets and other fintechs (named category in MA 10-K Item 1): branded checkout, Venmo and Braintree compete for e-commerce and P2P payment flows, and route over cards, account-to-account rails or its own balances. It is also a customer of the card networks.

competitors.name: UPI (India, NPCI); alternative real-time account-based rail
competitors.why: Government-backed digital public infrastructure named in MA 10-K Item 1 (UPI, Pix, FedNow); replaces card payments for domestic person-to-merchant and P2P flows in India. Not a listed company; no financials.

competitors.name: Pix (Banco Central do Brasil); alternative real-time rail
competitors.why: Government instant payment system named in MA 10-K Item 1; competes for Brazilian domestic P2P and P2M, where MA has a functional currency (Brazilian real). Not a listed company; no numbers saved by this lane.

competitors.name: FedNow (US Federal Reserve); alternative real-time rail
competitors.why: US instant account-to-account rail named in MA 10-K Item 1; potential competitor for US P2P and bill pay, early scale. Not a listed company; no numbers saved by this lane.

competitors.name: Stablecoin payment rails (GENIUS Act regulated); alternative
competitors.why: Digital currencies named in MA 10-K Item 1 as both an opportunity and a competitor for cross-border and B2B payments; MA is embedding them (Mastercard Move, ~130 crypto co-brand card programs per 10-K). Not a company; no numbers saved.

bottlenecks.reading: What MA supplies: a global four-party authorization, clearing and settlement network with trust, fraud and tokenization on top; the scarce thing is accepted-everywhere trust and issuer and merchant coverage (network effects), not capacity. Capacity is not the constraint; the constraint on growth is volume of spend and pricing versus customer incentives. 2025 payment network net revenue 19,476M (+12%) after rebates and incentives of 20,522M (+16%): incentives grow faster than network revenue.

Cross-border is the highest-yield flow in the network: 2025 cross-border assessments 12,021M (+18%, +17% currency-neutral) against domestic assessments 11,029M (+8%); Q3 2026 cross-border volume +11% local currency, gross dollar volume +7%, switched transactions +9%. Visa reports cross-border +14% in its FQ4 2026, so MA's cross-border growth was below Visa's in the latest quarter (different quarter windows: MA Jul-Sep 2026, Visa Jul-Sep 2026 volume).

Value-added services and solutions is the second engine: 2025 net revenue 13,315M (+23%, +21% currency-neutral, of which 3 points from acquisitions) versus payment network +12%; drivers named in the 10-K are security, digital and authentication, consumer acquisition and engagement, pricing and insights. Competitors named are consultancies, cyber and fraud technology firms and loyalty providers.

Real-time account-to-account rails are the structural threat to domestic card volume in markets where they are state-backed: UPI alone cleared 24.07 billion transactions in Sep 2026 (+23% year over year, NPCI via press). MA's 10-K says local debit brands and DPI mainly leave MA with cross-border there; how much domestic spend is displaced is not quantified in MA's own numbers.

Pix, FedNow and stablecoin rail volumes: web search gave conflicting figures (Pix about 7 billion transactions a month; FedNow about 5.0 million in Q2 2026 versus other counts; stablecoin payments between about 0.4 and 1.8 trillion USD depending on definition). Not primary data; kept as a hypothesis that FedNow is still immaterial against card volume and that stablecoin definition drives the size.

notes: fd NAMED COMPETITORS (10-K Item 1, pf_10k_20260211): General Purpose Payments Networks: Visa, American Express, JCB, China UnionPay, Discover; Debit and Local Networks: ATM/POS debit networks, local domestic brands; Real-time Account-based: ACH and real-time providers; Digital Wallets and Fintechs: wallets, BNPL, mobile operators, B2B AP/AR providers (PayPal is the listed example in the run's competitor list, not named by MA); DPI/government: Pix, FedNow, UPI, CBDCs; Digital Currencies: stablecoins, crypto; Services and Solutions: information and consulting firms, cyber and fraud technology, loyalty providers, open finance.

fd SHARE MA net revenue 2025 32,791M (+16%) versus Visa fiscal 2025 40,000M (+11.3%, pf_peer_V) and Visa fiscal 2026 45.9B (+15%, fd_v_rel_fy26q4): MA's latest comparable quarter growth was 14% (Q3 2026, pf_rel_20261029_1) against Visa's 13% (FQ4 2026): MA and Visa are growing at about the same rate, so no clear share shift between the two from revenue; windows are the same calendar quarter (Jul-Sep 2026) but MA's revenue is net of larger incentives, so revenue is not a volume-share measure.

fd SHARE Operating margin: MA 2025 GAAP 57.6% (adjusted 59.2%, 10-K) and Q3 2026 59.8% (pf_rel_20261029_1); Visa fiscal 2025 59.98% and fiscal 2026 about 61.2% GAAP (derived), so Visa runs a higher margin on a larger base.

fd SHARE Volumes: MA Q3 2026 gross dollar volume +7% local currency, cross-border +11%; Visa FQ4 2026 payments volume +9% constant dollar, cross-border +14%. On these numbers Visa grew volume faster than MA in the same quarter (different measure definitions: GDV includes cash, Visa payments volume excludes cash), a hypothesis of modest Visa share gain, not a measured share.

fd SHARE AXP billed business Q3 2026 +8% (fd_axp_q3_26, search summary), AXP revenue +9%; PayPal revenue +2% and transaction margin dollars +2% (fd_pypl_q3_26): MA is growing faster than both on revenue; AXP and PayPal are not taking network share from MA on these numbers.

fd SHARE Alternative rails: UPI +23% year over year in transaction count (Sep 2026); no MA-own number measures the displacement, labelled hypothesis that domestic card volume growth in India is capped while cross-border and VAS carry MA's growth there.
